note: The §4 normative matrix — one row per crash/fault point. F1/F2/F6/F8 are the accepted machinery (workspace §5.1/§6.3/§7.5/§13.5); F3/F7 are the packet-65/66 surfaces; F4/F5 are the 67 operations. Every row: the on-disk state, the detection, the recovery, and the original-preservation outcome.

rows.state: the pre-write envelope intact (the §5.1 atomic W: temp + rename + fsync — a torn write is impossible)
rows.detection: open: the load pipeline succeeds at the previous revision (no error)
rows.originals: intact (the envelope is either the old or the new whole document — §5.5)

rows.fault: crash between claim-file create and content write
rows.state: orphan claim file at the target epoch
rows.recovery: operator file operation (prove the holder dead, remove the orphan claim file, re-issue the open — the accepted error hint; NO backend command)

rows.fault: crash in a template phase (packet 65 §5: reserved/blobs/envelope/replayed)
rows.state: the reservation marker + the partial per-phase state
rows.detection: open/scan: template_initialization_incomplete (the phase is recorded in the marker)
rows.recovery: resume (the operator re-issues the same createProjectFromTemplate call — the dedup-safe deterministic requestIds) or delete the destination (operator file op)
rows.originals: the template sources and every other project untouched (the destination is the only partial)

rows.state: a partial destDir without a valid backup-manifest.json (the manifest is written last)
rows.detection: every 67 tool: backup_incomplete (the manifest is the gate)
rows.recovery: delete-and-recreate (the tool refuses the nonempty destination — no merge, no partial adoption)
rows.originals: the source project byte-identical (the backup is read-only on the source)

rows.detection: the tool: restore_destination_nonempty on the re-run (the destination guard, checked before the first write)
rows.recovery: delete the destination (operator file op), re-run from the verified backup
rows.originals: the source backup and every existing project untouched

rows.fault: disk/write fault during any durable write
rows.state: the W procedure surfaces the fault; the file is either the old or the new whole document
rows.detection: the operation's failure code (content_publish_failed / the write-fault class); the envelope last-written hash check on next open
rows.recovery: the accepted retry/takeover rules; no operator file op beyond the accepted claim rules

rows.fault: a kit file tampered between vendor and use (66)
rows.state: the vendored kit ≠ its kit.json identity
rows.detection: the game-build tool's pre-build re-hash (before the pin comparison — a tampered kit is refused regardless of the pin)
rows.recovery: re-vendor the pinned kit (the operator re-assembles from the kit identity)
rows.originals: the game project + game.json untouched (the refusal is before any build output)

rows.state: the catalog digest ≠ the file hash
rows.detection: contentIntegrity (open/scan): blob_corrupt for the named version
rows.recovery: the accepted §13.5 handling; a backup taken before the rot restores the bytes (the blob is the recoverable class)
rows.originals: the envelope intact (the manifest + envelope are untouched by blob rot)

invariant: no-ready-partial (C09): no fault point leaves a destination that opens as valid while actually partial — every partial state is detected with a named code before any valid-open claim.
